transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Alex Chen (Meridian CISO), Priya Kaur (Meridian Security Eng), Tom Barker (Meridian IT Ops)

[00:00:00] Samantha: hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got about 45 minutes blocked to walk through Redwood's audit logs and admin activity capture. diego and i will cover the event types, export options, retention, and encryption. alex, priya, anything specific you want on the agenda?
[00:00:20] Alex: yeah thanks sam, main things for us are: what do you actually capture, can we stream to our SIEM, retention limits, and key control. also need to understand how this ties to our SSO identities.
[00:00:35] Diego: great, we'll start high level then show examples. quick note - transcription may mess up some product names, like Redwood Dedictated in the notes, so apologies in advance.
[00:00:50] Priya: that's fine, just want the specifics.
[00:01:10] Diego: ok first, event categories we capture: admin console actions (user create/update/delete), role and permission changes, SSO/SCIM provisioning events, API key creation and rotation, model deployments and rollouts, inference endpoint changes, billing access events, and security policy changes. we also log system events like node restarts, autoscaler actions, and KV cache (sometimes transcribed as K-V cash) evictions which can be useful for incident forensics.
[00:01:45] Tom: that KV cache item is interesting for performance incidents. do you capture request IDs for each generation?
[00:01:55] Samantha: yes we include correlation IDs/request IDs per request, and they show up in the log event so you can tie model outputs back to the request and user.
[00:02:20] Alex: what fields are in each event? timestamp, actor, action, resource, request_id, region?
[00:02:30] Diego: exactly. typical schema: timestamp, event_type, actor_id (SSO principal if available), source_ip, resource_id (e.g., endpoint or model), action (create/update/delete/rotate/deploy), request_id, request_latency, outcome (success/failure), and metadata blob with request payload hashes and model hash. we also include approximate token counts for generation events.
[00:03:05] Priya: do you capture prompt text or embeddings? that's a data privacy concern.
[00:03:12] Diego: good question. by default audit events do not store full prompt text; we capture metadata and hashes. for customers who opt in we can include truncated or redacted content via explicit configuration, but that's not on by default for privacy reasons.
[00:03:30] Alex: how long are these logs kept by default?
[00:03:36] Samantha: default retention for hosted accounts is 90 days. enterprise customers can configure longer retention or archive to your S3/GCS bucket for indefinite storage.
[00:03:50] Tom: ok archive to our S3 - can we apply lifecycle rules and encryption on our side?
[00:03:58] Diego: yes, you can stream via S3 export and then manage lifecycle and S3 encryption. we sign the upload and you can have server-side encryption with your KMS. we also offer direct syslog and webhook streaming to SIEMs like Splunk or Datadog.
[00:04:20] Priya: do you support bringing our own KMS keys (BYOK)?
[00:04:26] Samantha: yes for Private and Dedicated customers we support BYOK/HSM integrations and customer-managed keys for both data-at-rest and for exported archives. for hosted we offer integration with cloud KMS and enterprise can work with us on a dedicated key.
[00:04:45] Alex: is there an immutable log store? we need tamper-evidence for audits.
[00:04:51] Diego: we provide append-only log storage with write-once semantics internally; for exports we can stream to an object store with versioning enabled. we also provide SHA256 hashes per batch and an audit chain that can be used to verify integrity. it's not a blockchain, but it is tamper-evident for audit purposes.
[00:05:20] Tom: how are logs protected in transit?
[00:05:25] Samantha: TLS 1.2/1.3 for in-transit; mutual TLS for certain enterprise integrations like syslog over mTLS.
[00:05:35] Alex: about SSO/identities, how do you map events to our IdP?
[00:05:40] Diego: we integrate via SAML/SCIM. when SCIM provisioning is enabled we map SCIM groups to RBAC roles and we log the SCIM user_id and email as actor_id in events. if SCIM is absent we fallback to internal user IDs.
[00:06:00] Priya: are there examples of the raw export format? JSON lines or CSV?
[00:06:06] Diego: exports are JSON lines (one event per line) with a documented schema. we can provide example files. syslog will be RFC5424-ish formatted with the event payload as JSON. webhooks post JSON to your endpoint.
[00:06:30] Alex: latency - if we stream to our SIEM, how close to real time is it?
[00:06:35] Samantha: near-real time, generally sub-10s for webhook/syslog, S3 uploads may be batched (minute-level) depending on throughput and your config.
[00:06:50] Tom: is PII redaction available?
[00:06:54] Diego: we provide configurable redaction and tokenization options; by default PII fields are not stored in full in audit logs. for compliance you can ask for regex-based redaction rules.
[00:07:10] Alex: retention and legal holds - can you put holds on certain accounts?
[00:07:15] Samantha: yes enterprise can request legal holds and we support retention locks for archives streamed to customer-managed buckets. we also have a policy where retention adjustments for hosted accounts require contract addendums.
[00:07:34] Priya: regarding SOC2 and ISO - can you share the reports?
[00:07:38] Samantha: absolutely, we'll send SOC 2 Type II and ISO summary docs; those are available under NDA if needed.
[00:07:47] Diego: also we have a security whitepaper that details our logging pipeline and separation of duties.
[00:07:55] Alex: regarding event scoping - will you capture model rollout variants, canary switches, and automatic fallback events?
[00:08:03] Diego: yes, rollout events, canary deploy status, and automatic fallback triggers are logged with the rollout id, previous and new model refs, and reason codes.
[00:08:20] Tom: what about retention of system-level telemetry vs admin audit events - are they separated?
[00:08:27] Diego: yes we separate operational telemetry (metrics/traces) from audit logs. audit logs are designed for security/compliance and have stronger access controls; telemetry is aggregated and sampled.
[00:08:46] Priya: access controls - who at Redwood can see raw logs?
[00:08:50] Samantha: access is role-based internally, and access to customer logs is limited to a small ops/security group under strict approvals; we can provide a matrix of who has access.
[00:09:03] Alex: can we receive alerts on admin activity, e.g., API key rotations or large role changes?
[00:09:08] Diego: yes we support alerting hooks and can trigger webhooks on defined event patterns. you can also stream to your SIEM and create alerts there.
[00:09:20] Alex: ok for the pilot - we'd like a sample export with a week of typical events and the schema. we also want to see how request_id ties to inference logs.
[00:09:29] Samantha: we'll do that. diego will prepare a sample and include request_id examples and linking instructions.
[00:09:40] Diego: i'll include a small dataset (jsonl) with events spanning admin actions, model deploys, api key rotations, and a couple of inference request linkages.
[00:09:56] Tom: do you charge extra for log exports or long-term archiving?
[00:10:02] Samantha: for hosted accounts exports are included but enterprise/archive beyond standard storage can have additional fees; for Dedicated/Private we have options in the contract. we'll include pricing in the follow-up.
[00:10:20] Alex: compliance - can you provide an audit trail for role changes that include who approved them?
[00:10:26] Diego: yes role-change events include actor, timestamp, approver_id if available (we can capture approval workflow metadata via our integration with your ticketing/approval system if you enable it).
[00:10:44] Priya: any limitations on event volume?
[00:10:48] Samantha: practical limits depend on plan; we can support high-volume streaming for enterprise, and batching strategies exist to avoid throughput bottlenecks. we'll dimension during the pilot.
[00:11:05] Alex: do you keep logs for failed login attempts to the console?
[00:11:09] Diego: yes failed auth attempts, unusual IPs, and MFA events are all logged.
[00:11:20] Tom: about schema changes - how do you communicate if you change event schemas?
[00:11:24] Diego: we version the schema, publish changelogs, and provide a migration guide. exports include schema_version metadata so you can handle changes programmatically.
[00:11:40] Priya: we need proof for auditors that logs are complete - can you provide export manifests and checksums?
[00:11:47] Samantha: yes, export manifests with batch checksums and sequence IDs are provided; they can be used to verify integrity and completeness.
[00:12:05] Alex: anything else about multi-region or data residency?
[00:12:10] Diego: we can restrict where logs are stored; for Private deployments you keep everything in your VPC/region. hosted customers can select region and we can route exports to customer buckets in specific regions for sovereignty.
[00:12:28] Tom: are there demo links or docs you can share?
[00:12:31] Samantha: we'll share the security whitepaper, SOC2 report, schema doc, and a sample jsonl export. expect those in the next two business days.
[00:12:45] Alex: excellent. on the legal hold - could that be automated via API?
[00:12:50] Diego: yes we have APIs to tag and lock exports; for hosted plans, automated holds require enterprise add-on.
[00:13:05] Priya: one last question - do you integrate with our ticketing system to surface suspicious admin changes?
[00:13:11] Diego: yes we have webhook connectors and can push to Jira/ServiceNow with event payloads and include remediation playbooks.
[00:13:28] Samantha: ok let's recap next steps - we'll send SOC2 & whitepaper, diego will prepare sample export, and we schedule the pilot. any blockers from your side?
[00:13:38] Alex: no blockers, just internal signoff and legal on the NDA for SOC docs.
[00:13:46] Priya: we'll send retention constraints after the call.
[00:13:51] Samantha: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up via email with attachments and a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff.

Notes/imperfections: occasional transcript typos (e.g., Redwood Dedictated, K-V cash), speaker attribution may be slightly off in a few lines.

End of transcript.
